provenance.authorship: Authored from the public two-rule contract without inspecting the checker implementation.
provenance.limitations: Small, intentionally labeled syntax examples. Not an external benchmark, real-world accuracy estimate, exploitability test, or security clearance. Cases cease to be held out when used for development.

cases.source: process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = '0';
cases.rationale: An unshadowed global process receives the exact disabling string.

cases.source: process['env']['NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED'] = '0';
cases.rationale: Static string-bracket notation denotes the same supported environment assignment.

cases.source:
import client from 'node:https';
client.request({ rejectUnauthorized: false });
cases.rationale: An unchanged default builtin import receives an unambiguous direct literal option.

cases.source:
import * as secureClient from 'node:https';
secureClient['get']({ ['rejectUnauthorized']: false });
cases.rationale: Static bracket names preserve the direct builtin call and option identity.

cases.source:
import { Agent as ClientAgent } from 'node:https';
new ClientAgent({ rejectUnauthorized: false });
cases.rationale: The named builtin Agent constructor uses a direct literal disabling option.

cases.source:
const client = require('node:https');
client.request({ rejectUnauthorized: false });
cases.rationale: An unchanged CommonJS builtin module binding is a supported direct-call form.

cases.source:
const { get: fetchSecure } = require('node:https');
fetchSecure({ rejectUnauthorized: false });
cases.rationale: Destructuring renames a supported builtin method without changing its identity.

cases.source:
import { connect as connectSecure } from 'node:tls';
connectSecure({ rejectUnauthorized: false });
cases.rationale: The builtin TLS connect call directly supplies the disabling option.

cases.source: process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = '1';
cases.rationale: The exact literal is not the disabling value. This is not a whole-file security claim.

cases.source: const previousSetting = process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED;
cases.rationale: Reading the environment property does not perform the matched assignment.

cases.source:
// process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = '0';
const documentation = "client.request({ rejectUnauthorized: false })";
cases.rationale: Comments and ordinary strings are inert syntax, not matched operations.

cases.source:
import client from 'node:https';
client.request({ rejectUnauthorized: true });
cases.rationale: The direct literal explicitly enables the relevant validation option.

cases.source:
const tls = require('node:tls');
tls.connect({ rejectUnauthorized: true });
cases.rationale: A supported TLS call with the enabled literal is not the disabling pattern.

cases.source: const displaySettings = { rejectUnauthorized: false };
cases.rationale: An unconsumed object property alone does not identify a builtin TLS operation.

cases.source:
import https from './display-client.js';
https.request({ rejectUnauthorized: false });
cases.rationale: A local variable name does not convert a non-builtin import into node:https.

cases.source:
import client from 'node:https';
client.request({});
cases.rationale: An empty direct options literal contains neither a disabling option nor an override.

cases.source: const enabled: boolean = true;
cases.rationale: TypeScript is outside the documented JS/MJS/CJS syntax surface.

cases.source: const view = <section />;
cases.rationale: JSX is outside the documented syntax surface.

cases.source: const options = {;
cases.rationale: A parse failure must not become an assessed negative.

cases.source: function configure(process) { process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED = '0'; }
cases.rationale: The process identifier is a parameter; the contract requires an explicit binding-uncertainty gap.
Reassignment prevents the checker from treating the call as an unchanged builtin binding.

cases.source:
import client from 'node:https';
client.request({ rejectUnauthorized: false, ...settings });
cases.rationale: A later spread may override the disabling property; the supported contract abstains.

cases.source:
import client from 'node:https';
client.request({ rejectUnauthorized: false, rejectUnauthorized: true });
cases.rationale: Duplicate override resolution is outside the no-override literal contract and must not silently clear the case.
The checker does not propagate object values into calls; indirect options require a coverage gap.
